Let $M = \min_{J \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}} f(J)$. Since the set of values $\{f(I) \mid I \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\}$ includes the value $M$, there exists at least one subset $J^0$ such that $f(J^0) = M$.

Assuming the family is non-trivial so that $M > 0$, we can divide both sides by $M$:
$$ k \geq 1. $$
